title: Cooling Fan Not Operating
summary: Diagnostic path for radiator fan no-operation, overheating at idle, A/C warm at idle, relays, fuses, fan command, and motor checks.
intro: A cooling fan fault should be split into command, power, ground, relay/fuse, motor, sensor input, and airflow problems. Do not replace the fan assembly until command and circuit behavior are confirmed.
common_sounds: Overheats in traffic but cools while driving
Fan never comes on or only one fan operates
quick_checks: Verify coolant level and actual engine temperature before electrical testing
Command the fan with a scan tool when supported
Check fan fuses, relays, control module, power feed, and ground under load
Check ECT data plausibility and A/C pressure request inputs
Backprobe motor current draw or voltage drop before condemning the fan assembly
common_causes: Failed fan motor or high-resistance fan connector
Blown fuse, failed relay, control module, or missing power feed
Poor ground or voltage drop in fan circuit
ECT sensor data, A/C pressure input, or PCM command issue
Blocked condenser/radiator airflow or damaged fan shroud

diagnostic_path_sections.title: Command Path
diagnostic_path_sections.summary: Find whether the PCM is requesting fan operation and why.
checks: Compare actual temperature to scan-tool ECT
Check fan command with A/C request
Review P0117, P0118, P0480, and pressure sensor data

diagnostic_path_sections.title: Power and Motor Path
diagnostic_path_sections.summary: If command exists, prove fuse, relay, feed, ground, and motor behavior under load.
checks: Load test fan power and ground
Check relay control and fuse voltage
Measure motor current draw if accessible

recommended_repairs.title: Radiator Fan Replacement
recommended_repairs.description: Use after command, fuse, relay, power, and ground checks confirm the fan motor or assembly.
